Genel Energy Reaches Revised $436 Million Cash Deal for Capricorn Energy
By Adam Whittaker
Genel Energy said it agreed to buy Capricorn Energy in a $436 million cash deal after hiking its offer price and outbidding Norway-listed DNO.

Genel said Friday that Capricorn shareholders would receive a cash payment of $5.74 for each share. This comprises $4.75 plus a special dividend of 99 cents. The offer represents a 63% premium to the stock's closing price on March 10, the last day before the first offer was made.

Genel and DNO have been competing to acquire the U.K.-based oil and gas exploration and production company. In mid-September, DNO revised the terms of its $396 million offer to make it an all-cash deal.

Genel said its new offer represents a roughly 10% premium to DNO's revised offer. Capricorn's management has withdrawn its recommendation that shareholders accept the DNO offer in favor of its own offer, Genel said.
